Plot rarefaction curves

Source: R/rarefaction_curve.r
plot.ecodive_rarefaction_curve.Rd

Draws the curves from rarefaction_curve(): one line per sample, of a metric against depth (or coverage), or of coverage against depth.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'ecodive_rarefaction_curve'
plot(
  x,
  metric = NULL,
  groups = NULL,
  data = NULL,
  type = "depth",
  depth = NULL,
  legend = "bottomright",
  col = NULL,
  ...
)

Arguments

x

The result of rarefaction_curve().

metric

Which of x's metrics to draw, by ID or name (matched as alpha_div() matches them). Default: the first in x.

groups

Colours the samples by group, with a legend, and draws each group's median curve as a thicker line: the name of a column of data, or a vector with one value per sample (all the samples in the totals attribute, matched by name when both are named, as for permanova()).

data

A data frame of sample metadata, with one row per sample (matched by row name, else in order), when groups names one of its columns.

type

What to draw: "depth" (the default), the metric against depth; "coverage", the metric against expected coverage (coverage-based rarefaction curves); or "completeness", expected coverage against depth (sample completeness curves, Chao et al. 2014, Fig. 4). A prefix is enough.

depth

A depth to mark with a vertical line (for type = "depth" or "completeness"), such as one you plan to rarefy to. It is labelled with how many of the samples have at least that many observations. Default: NULL (none).

legend

Where to put the legend of groups: a keyword for graphics::legend(), such as "bottomright" (the default), or NULL for none.

col

The lines' colours: one colour for every sample, or with groups, one per group (in order, or named by group). Defaults to grey without groups, and to grDevices::hcl.colors()'s "Dark 3" palette with them.

...

Passed on to graphics::plot.default(), such as main, sub, xlab, ylab, xlim, ylim or log. They replace the defaults made from x.

Value

x, invisibly.

Details

The title is "Rarefaction Curves of" and the metric's name (see list_metrics()), or "Sample Completeness Curves"; the subtitle says how the values were made: "Expected values" for a closed form, or, for instance, "Mean of 10 rarefactions". A group's median curve is the median of its samples' values at each depth that at least two of them share (or every depth, for a group of one); past a sample's library size, the sample has no value, so the median is over fewer samples (as QIIME 2's group medians).

References

Chao, A., Gotelli, N. J., Hsieh, T. C., Sander, E. L., Ma, K. H., Colwell, R. K., & Ellison, A. M. (2014). Rarefaction and extrapolation with Hill numbers: a framework for sampling and estimation in species diversity studies. Ecological Monographs, 84, 45–67. doi:10.1890/13-0133.1

Examples

    rc <- rarefaction_curve(ex_counts, c('observed', 'shannon'), times = 5)

    plot(rc, depth = 1000)

    plot(rc, 'shannon', groups = c('A', 'A', 'B', 'C'))

    plot(rc, type = 'coverage')

    plot(rc, type = 'completeness', main = 'How complete is each sample?')
